batch.title: Signs that contradict their own quote (16 Oct 2026)
batch.notes: Five units where the encoded direction, magnitude or comparator looks wrong against the quote itself. These are extraction defects rather than synthesis rules, so they need a human call before the next re-synthesis. Four were found by the agent that tagged gas and baseline; the fifth is a check that we read a genuine harm finding correctly.

units.citation: Santos et al. (2025). Sistemas Agroflorestais no Semiárido Brasileiro: Uma Revisão sobre Viabilidade, Benefícios Econômicos e Ecológicos. Revista Brasileira de Geografia Física.
units.quote: Verificaram valores de estoque de carbono no solo de 134,65; 97,59; 71,64 e 68,16 Mg ha-1 para vegetação natural, silvipastoril, agrossilvopastoril e sistema tradicional, respectivamente, representando um aumento de cerca de 7,68% para a vegetação natural e uma redução de 19,65; 6,68 e 46,34% para os sistemas, silvipastoril, agrossilvopastoril e sistema tradicional, quando comparado o início e final do banco de dados avaliados. (English: They found soil carbon stock values of 134.65; 97.59; 71.64 and 68.16 Mg ha-1 for natural vegetation, silvopastoral, agrosilvopastoral and traditional systems respectively, representing an increase of about 7.68% for natural vegetation and a reduction of 19.65; 6.68 and 46.34% for the silvopastoral, agrosilvopastoral and traditional systems, when comparing the beginning and end of the datasets assessed.)

relationship.outcome_raw: soil carbon stocks higher and losses smaller under silvopastoral and agrosilvopastoral systems than the traditional slash-and-burn system after 13 years

context.note: values printed with decimal commas (134,65; 97,59; 71,64; 68,16 Mg/ha) so not machine-recordable

units.question: Recorded as a carbon GAIN, but the quote shows the silvopastoral system LOSING 19.65% of its soil carbon while natural vegetation gained 7.68%. It is positive only against a slash-and-burn arm the claim never names. Should the sign be flipped, or the comparator stated?

plain.described: The source's own description of the practice was not captured for this unit (it is required from ruleset v1.6.9 on) — read the quote and say whether what was measured really is this practice.

band.rule: the unit records a direction but no size, so no band applies and the row's strength rests on the other units in the cell

units.citation: Ojanen et al. (2020). Rewetting Offers Rapid Climate Benefits for Tropical and Agricultural Peatlands But Not for Forestry‐Drained Peatlands. Global Biogeochemical Cycles.
units.quote:
In temperate and boreal
agricultural peat soils, the warming effect of methane emissions offsets a major part of the cooling for the
ﬁrst decades after rewetting.

relationship.outcome_raw: temperate and boreal AGRICULTURAL peat soils: the warming from the increased METHANE emissions offsets a MAJOR PART of the cooling from the avoided CARBON DIOXIDE for the first decades after rewetting — the benefit is real but heavily eroded by methane outside the tropics

context.practice_as_described: rewetting of peat soils drained for agriculture and forestry — 'Peatland is rewetted by blocking ditches'; scenarios cover tropical cropland and plantation peat soils, temperate and boreal agricultural peat soils, and temperate and boreal forestry-drained peat soils, with the forestry cases split by whether trees are clear-cut or abandoned at rewetting
context.note: 100-year radiative-forcing scenarios built from IPCC Wetlands Supplement emission factors as revised by Wilson et al. (2016), with a Finnish tree-biomass and wood-product case study; global coverage, no single study country; climate_zone recorded as temperate although the claim covers temperate AND boreal, which the single-valued vocabulary cannot express | gas/baseline tag 2026-10-16: the warming effect of methane emissions offsets a major part of the cooling for the first decades after rewetting

units.question: Recorded as NEGATIVE for 'methane offsets a major part of the cooling'. That is an eroded net benefit, not a reversal — compare the sibling unit where the offset exceeds 100% and negative is right. As encoded it votes against rewetting on a sentence that still describes net cooling.

units.citation: kumwimba et al. (2024). Nutrient and sediment retention by riparian vegetated buffer strips: Impacts of buffer length, vegetation type, and season. Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment.
units.quote:
For an 18 m RVBS (Fig. 5), the 
woody treatment achieved removal efficiencies of 89.8% for TN, 90.2% 
for NO3-N, 93.7% for NH4-N, and 58% for TP, DP and PO4-P.

relationship.outcome_raw: total nitrogen removal efficiency of an 18 m woody riparian buffer strip (NO3-N 90.2%, NH4-N 93.7%, and 58% for the P species in the same sentence)

context.practice_as_described: riparian vegetated buffer strips along the Guishui River: 'preexisting or well-established, unmanaged buffers composed of herbaceous/grasses, woody, and shrub vegetation', likely in place for over 10 years, about 3.0 m wide and 2-18 m long, compared with a bare-ground 'no buffer strip' control, below cropland of orchards and vegetable fields under traditional tillage
context.note: the 58% P figure in this sentence disagrees with the 92.8% TP figure reported for the same treatment on the same page - an internal inconsistency in the paper, flagged not resolved

units.question: The source reports BOTH 58% and 92.8% total-phosphorus removal for the same 18 m woody treatment on the same page. Which is the claim, and is the other a different measure (concentration vs mass)?

units.citation: Allan et al. (2023). Meta‐analysis reveals that enhanced practices accelerate vegetation recovery during peatland restoration. Restoration Ecology.
units.quote:
Enhanced restoration led reliably to intact levels of peatland specialist plant diversity within ~8 
246 
years, while stressor removal (basic restoration) appeared to cause a decline in peatland 
247 
specialist diversity. The mean response of peatland specialist diversity to passive restoration on 
248 
average was again slightly negative. However, the character of these responses could not be 
249 
predicted with high confidence (Figure 3d).

relationship.outcome_raw: peatland specialist plant DIVERSITY under BASIC restoration (stressor removal) - appeared to cause a DECLINE, and the mean response under passive restoration was slightly negative; the authors state these responses could not be predicted with high confidence

context.practice_as_described: peatland restoration coded at three intensities: 'passive restoration (cessation of the degrading activity with no active restoration)'; basic/standard restoration = 'removal of stressors' such as 'rewetting, tree felling'; and 'enhanced restoration (such as active revegetation)', in particular the Moss Layer Transfer Technique (MLTT), which reintroduces Sphagnum mosses to the surface
context.note: REVERSAL kept: rewetting alone, without active revegetation, is reported here as reducing peatland specialist diversity. Low confidence per the authors, hence significance=ns.

units.question: Kept deliberately as a measured decline caused by basic rewetting (NOT a shortfall against an intact reference, so it still votes). Confirm that reading: the authors' own confidence is low and the result is not significant.
